metadata.title: Japan’s newly crowned top company gets a downgrade on AI ‘mania’ concerns - MarketWatch

content.text:
The Ratings Game
Japan’s newly crowned top company gets a downgrade on AI ‘mania’ concerns
SoftBank overtook Toyota on Monday on the market-cap table
Through its control of U.K. microprocessor designer Arm Holdings and its investment in ChatGPT maker OpenAI, the Japanese investment group SoftBank has nearly quintupled in value over the past year, and on Monday it became the country’s largest company, overtaking Toyota.
Now, one analyst has had enough. Deutsche Bank analyst Peter Milliken downgraded SoftBank’s stock from buy to hold while nudging up his price target to 8,700 yen from 8,600 yen. SoftBank JP:9984 on Tuesday rose another 1%, to 8,632 yen.
About the Author
Steven Goldstein is based in London and responsible for MarketWatch's coverage of financial markets in Europe, with a particular focus on global macro and commodities. Previously, he was Washington bureau chief, directing MarketWatch's economic, political and regulatory coverage. Follow Steve on Twitter: @MKTWgoldstein.
